deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The bundle and the neighbouring pages (relations for (23), (23)^2 with Δ_2, Δ_3, and quotients like 24/(12·14)) point to the theory of Abelian functions for p=3, i.e. the 28 bitangents of a plane quartic. In Hesse's labelling these bitangents are the pairs (ij) of eight symbols. On this page the eight symbols are 1 and the seven labels 2,…,8. The seven labels are attached to the lines of a Fano plane, whose points are the indices 1,…,7 of parameters α_i, m_i. Riemann writes the bitangent quantities (1X) and (XY) as rational expressions in these 14 parameters.

(a) Normalised binary bilinear forms (top left). I read the symbol transcribed '5' as ζ. The forms are:
  (1) = ζ - z;
  Q_i(ζ,z) = (ζ-α_i)(z-α_i)/m_i + ζ - z, for i = 1, 2, ….
Write B = aζz + bζ + cz + d with determinant ad - bc. My own check (not on the page): every Q_i has determinant 1, and so does ζ - z. The polarised invariant of Q_i and Q_j is 2 + (α_i-α_j)^2/(m_i m_j). The page then sets (12) = δ_2. Presumably (1X) = δ_X for all X; I cannot see from the page how δ is defined.

(b) The combinatorial tables.
- The 5-row table lists seven columns {1234},{1256},{1278},{1357},{1368},{1467},{1458}. These are the seven blocks through 1 of the Steiner system S(3,4,8) (the planes of AG(3,2) through a point). Deleting 1 leaves the Fano plane on {2,…,8}.
- The right-hand table is a second Fano plane on the points 1,…,7, whose lines carry the labels 2,…,8: 2↔{1,2,3}, 3↔{1,4,5}, 6↔{2,5,6}, 7↔{3,4,6}, 4↔{1,6,7}, 5↔{2,4,7}, 8↔{3,5,7}. I checked that every pair of points lies on exactly one of these lines.

(c) Formula for (23). Riemann first writes (23) = ½δ_2δ_3·Σ, with Σ a sum of partial-fraction terms in m_1,…,m_5 and α_1,…,α_5. He rewrites this as
  Σ = (m1-m2)/(α1-α2) + (m1-m3)/(α1-α3) + (m1-m4)/(α4-α1) + (m1-m5)/(α5-α1) - (m2-m3)/(α2-α3) + (m4-m5)/(α4-α5).
I verified this coefficient by coefficient:
- m2 term: -1/(α1-α2) - 1/(α2-α3) = (α1-α3)/((α2-α1)(α2-α3)).
- m3 term: (α1-α2)/((α3-α1)(α3-α2)).
- m4 term: (α5-α1)/((α4-α1)(α4-α5)).
- m5 term: (α4-α1)/((α5-α1)(α5-α4)).
- m1 term: [1/(α1-α2) - 1/(α1-α4)] + [1/(α1-α3) - 1/(α1-α5)] = (α2-α4)/((α1-α2)(α1-α4)) + (α3-α5)/((α1-α3)(α1-α5)).

Shorthand: ij := (m_i-m_j)/(α_i-α_j). This is a first divided difference and is symmetric, ij = ji. Then
  (23) = ½δ_2δ_3(12+13-14-15-23+45).

General rule (implicit on the page). Two labelled lines X={p,a,b} and Y={p,c,d} meet in the point p. Then
  (XY) = ½δ_Xδ_Y(pa + pb - pc - pd - ab + cd) = ½δ_Xδ_Y(T_X(p) - T_Y(p)),
where T_L(p) = pa + pb - ab.

Riemann applies the rule to all pairs among the labels 2,3,6,7:
- (67): p=6 → 26+56-52-46-36+34;
- (27): p=3 → 32+31-12-36-34+46;
- (36): p=5 → 54+51-14-52-56+26;
- (26): p=2 → 23+21-13-25-26+56;
- (73): p=4 → 45+41-15-46-43+36.
All six agree with the rule.

The lines labelled 2,3,6,7 are exactly the four Fano lines missing the point 7, so they form a complete quadrilateral on the points 1,…,6. Each point is the meet of two of these lines: 1=2∩3, 2=2∩6, 3=2∩7, 4=3∩7, 5=3∩6, 6=6∩7. The three opposite (diagonal) point pairs are 16, 24 and 35, and these three symbols never occur.

(d) Lower half: an expansion of products. Each expression splits as S_{XY} = T_X(p) - T_Y(p), and Riemann multiplies these pieces across the three complementary products (23)(67), (26)(37), (27)(36). These products all carry the same factor ¼δ_2δ_3δ_6δ_7. Presumably he is testing a three-term relation among them, of the kind behind the representation √(p1p2)+√(p3p4)+√(p5p6)=0 of the quartic by bitangents. The target is not stated, so this is my inference.
- He lists cross terms such as -(12+13-23)(-46-36+34), -(26+56-52)(-14-15+45), (23+21-13)(-46-34+36), (-25-26+56)(45+41-15), -(12+13-23)(26+56-52) and (23+13-12)(-52-56+26).
- He regroups into six blocks of the shape -ab·cd + (pq-pr)(st-su): -46·12+(36-34)(23-13), -13·56+(26-25)(23-21), -23·45+(12-13)(15-14), -14·26+(54-51)(56-52), -15·36+(46-43)(45-41), -25·34+(64-63)(65-62).
- Each block's product term pairs two edges forming a perfect matching of four non-diagonal points.
- A further regrouping follows: (46-36)(26-56) + 46(-12+45-41) + 36(23-13-15) + 26(23-21-14) + 56(54-51-13).
- Finally he writes out the last block's factor explicitly: ((m6-m4)/(α6-α4) - (m6-m3)/(α6-α3))·((m6-m2)/(α6-α2) - (m6-m5)/(α6-α5)), i.e. (64-63)(62-65). Each bracket is a difference of divided differences, (α4-α3)·[6,4,3] and (α2-α5)·[6,2,5]. This suggests he wanted the result in terms of second divided differences.
The lower half breaks off without a stated conclusion.
errors: As transcribed, the first m1 term has denominator (α1-α4)(α4-α2). This is inconsistent with the next line; the denominator must be (α1-α2)(α1-α4). It is most likely a misreading or a writing slip.

The signs of several cross terms in the product expansion do not match any single combination ±S23·S67 ± S27·S36 ± S26·S37 that I could fix with certainty. The page looks like exploratory bookkeeping rather than a finished computation.

The block sums are not checkable as a finished identity. With all 12 symbols ij set to 1, every S_XY vanishes but the six blocks sum to -6. So the blocks cannot be just a quadratic combination of the S's; other terms (e.g. involving the δ's) or a different target must be intended. The page gives no conclusion.

results.what: Rational parametrisation of bitangent-type quantities: (1X)=δ_X and (XY)=½δ_Xδ_Y(pa+pb-pc-pd-ab+cd), indexed by a Fano plane, with ij=(m_i-m_j)/(α_i-α_j)
results.modern_name: Parametrisation of the 28 bitangents of a plane quartic (Hesse/Cayley pair labelling, Aronhold-set/Fano structure)
results.usually_credited_to: Hesse (1855) and Cayley for the 8-symbol labelling; Aronhold (1864) for the Aronhold set; Riemann (1864, published in the Werke) for the theta-function treatment

results.what: Partial-fraction rewriting of the sum for (23) into first divided differences
Tables: S(3,4,8) blocks through a point, and a Fano labelling of 7 lines by the labels 2..8
results.modern_name: Steiner system S(3,4,8) / Fano plane PG(2,2)

results.what: Attempted expansion of the products (23)(67), (27)(36), (26)(37) for the complete quadrilateral of lines 2,3,6,7
results.modern_name: Three-term relations among complementary bitangent products (Steiner complexes / syzygetic tetrads)
results.usually_credited_to: Steiner, Hesse (1850s); Riemann 1864 and Weber 1876 for the theta-relation form

deep.surprise_reason: Riemann's work on p=3 and the 28 bitangents with Aronhold/Fano combinatorics is known through his 1864 treatment edited by Weber. The specific rational parametrisation by the divided differences (m_i-m_j)/(α_i-α_j) is an unpublished detail of some interest. The page is exploratory and inconclusive.

transcription_corrections: The symbol transcribed '5' in the first lines is almost certainly ζ (zeta): (1)=ζ-z, 1=(1/m_1)(ζ-α_1)(z-α_1)+ζ-z, and likewise for 2.
The denominator of the first m1 term should read (α1-α2)(α1-α4), not (α1-α4)(α4-α2).
The fragments such as 'α1-α3 α1-α5' are products of two factors in the denominator: (α1-α3)(α1-α5), etc.
'26 / 73' are two separate left-hand sides: (26)=½δ2δ6(…) and (73)=(37)=½δ3δ7(…).
